body: claimed: issue-worker-high (claude-opus-5-5) · 2026-11-15T19:23Z · worktree/branch issue/1950-adaptive-stock-ring-budget · plan: measure the outline vertices and moves of the stock ring per level, then fix the cost in the HSM planner with a pinning test

Escalation: effort:high to effort:max. Claim released. Held work: branch `issue/1950-adaptive-stock-ring-budget`, commit f888c0766 (an ignored probe only, no fix).

**Readings** (release build, Windows). The probe is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_hsm_ring.rs`, test `probe_ring`. It builds the center area of one level as the 3-D ladder builds it: `open_sides` with the 70 x 70 stock, less the D part, eroded by r = 5.

- The center area has 4 pieces: a top U channel (area 877), the bore (177), and two bottom corner pieces (262 each).
- The ring splits where the part offset R35 touches the stock edge - 0.01, at the side midpoints. Each piece has zero-width wedge ends at those points.
- Whole level: refused after 237 revolutions, "~602.4 k outline vertices processed (limit 600 k)", in 8.4 s. This is the issue.
- The U piece is the second piece. It starts with an axial dive at (-7.78, 31.53). Its disc phase steps 0.001-0.01 mm per revolution for about 160 revolutions. That uses about 245 k vertices (40% of the budget).
- After the disc phase, growth is about 0.45 mm per revolution. Each revolution walks 600-750 mm of outline (about 5 k vertices).
- Each piece alone:
  - U (first piece, helix entry): completes in 16.1 s, 47,750 moves, rest 0.143.
  - Bore: 2.7 s, 3,284 moves, rest 0.
  - Each corner: 0.7 s, about 8 k moves, rest 0.361.
- Thus a completed plan also fails the rest law (HSM_REST_MAX 0.02). This agrees with "22% uncut at Z 0".

**What failed**

- GEOM_MAX raised to 600 M: no help. The work law (WORK_MAX) then refuses the level, at 37 s.
- The planner material clipped to the real stock (no band of air outside the stock): no help. Refused after 129 revolutions at 604.8 k vertices. The fronts stall in the wedges at steps of 0.04-0.12 mm.

A budget raise is therefore not a sound fix.

**Causes**

1. The #1774 footprint keeps the tool center inside the stock (edge - 0.01). The stock ring thus becomes narrow channels with zero-width wedge ends. In the wedges each approach overloads, the fronts crawl, and each revolution walks the full outline again (quadratic work).
2. The planner material (`comp.offset(r)`) includes a band of air about 5 mm wide outside the stock.
3. Each piece after the first starts with an axial dive (bore = r, no orbit). Its disc phase stalls for about 160 revolutions.

**Possible fix directions** (each changes posted G-code under the safety floor, in motion and app):

- Open-side planning: let the tool center go into the air outside the stock, and clip the material to the stock. The ring then has no wedges and the tool can enter from the air.
- Growth that knows wedges, and a disc phase that does not stall after an axial dive.

Probe command: `cargo test --release -p camcraft-motion --lib probe_ring -- --ignored --nocapture` (about 30 s).

claimed: issue-worker-max (claude-fable-5-2) · 2026-11-15T19:37Z · worktree/branch issue/1950-adaptive-stock-ring-budget · plan: plan the stock ring as an open pocket (tool centre in the air band outside the stock, material clipped to the stock, entry from the air side), with pinning tests

The maintainer stopped the worker at 2026-11-15T20:40Z, after about one hour of work. No fix exists yet. The local branch `issue/1950-adaptive-stock-ring-budget` (worktree `.claude/worktrees/issue-1950`) holds one commit, `f888c0766`: a held probe test of the stock-ring level for the HSM plan. The claim stays with the main session until the maintainer says how the work continues.

**Plan for the next worker (round 1 of 2: plan only, no code).** Source read: worktree `issue-1950` at `3bc839b2d` (main plus `f888c0766`).

## 1. Cause

- The budget that refuses the level is law 3 of `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/budget.rs`: `GEOM_MAX = 600_000` vertices (line 73) after `GEOM_LEN = 5_000` tool radii (line 78), checked in `Work::over` (lines 142-151). The probe reads 602.4 k vertices after 237 revolutions. When `GEOM_MAX` is raised, law 2 (`WORK_MAX = 30_000`, line 63) refuses the level. The move budget `MOVE_BUDGET = 120_000` (`pocket_hsm.rs:90`, checked in `over_budget`, line 100) is the second refusal in the issue body.
- The footprint is made in `crates/motion/src/machining3d/open_side.rs:42-53`. It grows (silhouette + stock outline) by `r - OPEN_SLACK` (`OPEN_SLACK = 0.01`, line 34). The ladder erodes the level target by `r` (`ladder.rs:133`). Thus the tool centre stops 0.01 mm inside the stock edge.
- On the D plate (R30 part, 70 x 70 stock, D10) the part offset R35 is 0.01 mm past the centre limit 34.99 at each side midpoint. The ring breaks into 4 pieces with zero-width wedge ends.
- `hsm_passes` (`pocket_hsm.rs:241-269`) plans each piece with the outward growth spiral (`adaptive/grow.rs`). That spiral grows from one entry disc, and each revolution walks the full cleared outline again. In a long channel with wedge ends the work is quadratic. Each piece after the first gets an axial dive (`pocket_hsm.rs:246-254`), and its disc phase stalls for about 160 revolutions.
- The planner material is `comp.offset(r)` (`pocket_hsm.rs:242`). It includes the air band outside the stock, so the planner cuts air as if it were stock.
- A budget that scales with the ring area is not a fix. The probe shows this: the U piece alone takes 16.1 s and leaves rest 0.143 (limit `HSM_REST_MAX = 0.02`, `pocket_hsm.rs:127`). I drop that option.
- A wider air band that removes the wedges, with the outward spiral kept, is also not a fix. The ring is then one area round the part island. Law 3's own calibration names the island case as the most expensive one (`budget.rs:69-72`: 865 k vertices for a 60 x 40 pocket round a 12 x 12 island). I drop that option too.

## 2. Recommended change: air-side rings (outside-in), not the growth spiral

When the stock outline is known, each point of the ring material is near air. Cut the ring from the air side inward, one front at a time, at the optimal load width `w = load * D` (1.46 mm for D10 at `DEFAULT_OPTIMAL_LOAD`). On the D plate that is about 10-12 fronts of at most 280 mm each: about 3-4 k mm of cut and less than 1 k r of planning work. That is far below each budget.

Function by function:

1. `machining3d::open_sides` (`open_side.rs`, about 10 lines): add a parameter `stock_band: f64`. The stock outline grows by `stock_band`. The silhouette grows by `r - OPEN_SLACK` as now. The app passes `2r + OPEN_SLACK` for the Adaptive strategy and `r - OPEN_SLACK` for each other strategy. Thus Offset rings and the other strategies keep their output.
2. `crates/app/src/operation/open_side.rs::open_footprint` (about 5 lines) and its two callers in `generate.rs` (lines 725, 1495): pass the band. For the Adaptive arm, also give the stock outline (`stock_region`) to the motion call.
3. `machining3d` entry (`entry.rs`, about 25 lines): add `pocket3d_open_prev(facets, footprint, stock: Option<&Region>, p, mask)`, and the rest variant if the Adaptive arm uses it. Do not change the signatures of the existing entry functions. `ladder::ladder` (`ladder.rs`) and `hsm::plan_level` (`hsm.rs:117`) take `stock: Option<&Region>` (about 10 lines). On the wrap (`seam` is `Some`), pass `None`.
4. `pocket_hsm::adaptive_passes` and `hsm_passes` (about 25 lines): take `stock: Option<&Region>`. When a stock is given, the material of each piece is `comp.offset(r)` intersected with the stock. If the centre area of the piece reaches past the stock outline (the piece has an air side), plan it with the new air-side planner. Else plan it as now (for example the bore).
5. New file `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_rings.rs` (about 200-250 lines, one concern), `pub(crate) fn plan_from_air(mat: &Region, center: &Region, s: &AdaptiveSpec) -> Result<AdaptivePlan, GenError>`:
   - Front k is the boundary of `M(k-1).offset(r - w)`, as a polyline. Keep only the runs inside `center`: sample at `seg = r/8` and split where a point is outside `center`.
   - Cut each run on the raster (`Raster::cut`, as `plan_within` does at `mod.rs:237`). Take the swept disc out of `mat` (the `take` law, `mod.rs:332-340`). Read each move with the same rim reading that `grow` uses for a trial. Keep the worst load.
   - Order: climb, front by front, outside-in. While a front is one closed loop, join it to the next front with `rings::morph_rev` over the last part of the revolution (one continuous inward spiral, no link). When a front breaks into open runs at the part wall, join run to run by a return on the cleared side (the previous front, reversed). Let `lift_returns` (`mod.rs:283`) make the microlift joins.
   - The first front starts from a plunge in the air band: the centre at `stock edge + r + 0.01`, the disc fully in air. Give `EntryRoom` that point with `helix_r = 0` (no helix in air).
   - Stop when `mat` has nothing left above the dust law of the planner, or when a front has no run inside `center`. Return `rest`, `travel` (`lift::travel`) and the worst-load note, as `plan_within` does.
   - If the worst load is more than `1 + PLAN_TOL` times the load, refuse by name (the existing fallback to Offset rings, with its note). Never a silent pass.
6. Provenance line for `air_rings.rs`: contour-parallel offsets of the cleared area (Held 1991, LNCS 500), the spiral between nested rings (Held and Spielberger 2009, CAD 41(7)), the engagement read on the in-process stock (Stori and Wright 2000). No vendor material.

Total: about 300-350 lines in motion, about 20 lines in app. `air_rings.rs` must stay below 400 lines.

## 3. Gouge safety

- The centre area is still `target.offset(-r)`, and `target` is still the footprint less the part material above Z (`ladder.rs:105-133`). The band grows only outside the stock outline, where there is no part material. `keep_out` (the other parts) is still taken out. Thus the tool centre stays a full radius off each part at each level.
- Each run is cut to `center` before it is posted. `plan_level` proves each fitted arc inside `center` (`fit_proved`, `hsm.rs:196`) and runs the crossing law (`crossing_free`).
- The material clip to the stock changes only what the planner reads as material. It never makes `center` larger.
- The entry plunge puts the disc fully in air outside the stock.
- The tool now goes up to `2r` past the stock side at the level Z. A vise jaw or a clamp on the stock side is in that band. The verify fixture law must block the post. No test builds that case today (PR #1780, "Not exercised"). Section 4 adds one pin for it.
- Existing pins of the gouge law: `pocket3d_open_side::stock_far_past_the_silhouette_is_cleared_to_the_stock_outline` (no cutter disc inside the part, verify clean), `level_links::a_helix_under_the_bore_floor_is_never_silent`, and the verify step of `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean`.

## 4. Tests

New pins:
- `adaptive::air_rings` lib tests:
  - `a_ring_round_an_island_is_cut_from_the_air_within_budget` (the probe level: no refusal, rest at most `HSM_REST_MAX`, moves below `MOVE_BUDGET`, worst load at most `1 + PLAN_TOL`);
  - `every_air_ring_pass_stays_in_the_centre_area`;
  - `the_air_entry_disc_is_clear_of_the_stock`;
  - `a_piece_with_no_air_side_keeps_the_growth_spiral`.
- Change the probe `pocket_hsm_ring.rs::probe_ring` into the pin `the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note`. Keep the fixture and remove the prints. If it takes more than 60 s in debug, put it in the heavy lane.
- `crates/app/tests/pocket3d_hsm.rs`: add the default case again (no Tool containment) as `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`: no "Offset rings cut" note, verify clean. Keep the Inside test of `bf752be65`.
- `pocket3d_open_side`: `a_non_adaptive_whole_model_keeps_the_old_band` (the Offset rings footprint does not change) and `a_clamp_in_the_air_band_blocks_the_post`.

Binaries to run (names only): camcraft-motion lib (modules `pocket_hsm`, `adaptive`, `machining3d`); camcraft-app `pocket3d_hsm`, `pocket3d_open_side`, `level_links`, `whole_model_pocket`, `operations`, `area_controls`, `keep_law`, `neighbour_law`, `adaptive_pinch`, `narrow_band`, `open_band`; clippy for `camcraft-motion` and `camcraft-app`.

## 5. Output changes

- Posted G-code changes for each whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy and a stock outline. The stock ring is cut outside-in from an entry in air, and the tool goes up to `2r` past the stock side. Multi-Axis Rough changes only if its arm uses Adaptive and passes the stock.
- There are no `tests/golden/` files for this path. The pinned move counts in the heavy lane of `pocket3d_hsm` change, and `stock_engine_agreement` can change. Update them at the cut, not in the PR.
- The Offset rings and the other strategies do not change (their band stays `r - OPEN_SLACK`).
- The `Changelog:` line must state the output change.

## 6. Leave out, and file as follow-up (`P7`, `source:agent`)

- The air-side planner for the stock outline of the 2D pocket (the #12 case).
- A step-in lead arc that is better than the microlift return, if the worst load at a run start is near the limit.
- The axial dive of later pieces (cause 3), for pieces that have no air side.
- A fixture-aware air band (a smaller band where a fixture is), if the fixture pin shows many refused posts.

## 7. Rounds (45 minutes each)

- **Round A (motion only):** `air_rings.rs` and its four lib tests, on hand-built regions (the probe fixture). Stop when the four tests are green in the quick gate, and the probe level shows no refusal and rest at most 0.02. No app change.
- **Round B (plumbing):** the `open_sides` band parameter, `pocket3d_open_prev`, the stock argument of `ladder`, `plan_level` and `hsm_passes`, and the app arm. Stop when `the_stock_ring_level_plans_adaptive_with_no_budget_note` and `a_non_adaptive_whole_model_keeps_the_old_band` are green, and the existing `pocket3d_open_side` and `level_links` suites are green.
- **Round C (app pins and PR):** `the_users_whole_model_bore_roughs_adaptive_on_each_level`, `a_clamp_in_the_air_band_blocks_the_post`, the touched app suites, clippy, the decision file `docs/decisions/1950-adaptive-stock-ring-air.md`, and the draft PR with a `Changelog:` line. Stop when the PR is open.

If round A shows a worst load at a run start above `1 + PLAN_TOL` that the microlift return cannot fix, stop after round A. Comment the readings and keep the issue at `effort:max`.

Decision record (for the decision file): chosen: air-side rings. Dropped: a budget raise (the probe shows that time and the rest law fail); a wider air band with the growth spiral (the island case of law 3); the planner material clip alone (the probe shows a refusal at 604.8 k).

**What is done (motion crate only)**

  - A front that the part wall breaks is cut as open runs. Each run starts with a lead-in that the planner measures step by step on the stock raster. If no lead-in keeps the load at the limit, the planner cuts the run short. The wall laps then remove that material.
  - Two wall laps, offset from the centre outline, come before the last lap on the outline.
- `Raster::open_air` marks the air band as open, not as wall. The scanline fill is now one function.

## What round C did

1. App arm. A whole-model 3D Pocket with the Adaptive strategy now uses the wide band (`stock_band(r, true)`). It calls `pocket3d_open_prev` with the setup stock outline. Shell, rest roughing and the other strategies keep the old band. Multi-Axis Rough keeps the old band too (an open choice). This changes the posted G-code of this operation.

3. Microlift joins (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/air_links.rs`). The air plan joins each pass to the pass before it with the existing `LinkLaw`: a straight chord, a return over the retract plane, or a lead whose graze joins the pass. Each join is walked again on the stock, and its readings go into the worst load. A pass with no proved join keeps its retract hop.
